title: Intelligence Brief
subtitle: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 launched at flat pricing, Researcher Chaofan Shou claims Kimi K3, coordinati, India's Cyber Crime Coordination Centre ordered Gi

insights.text: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 launched at flat pricing ($5/$25 per million input/output tokens, same as Opus 4.8), scoring three times the next-best model on ARC-AGI 3 and beating Fable 5's best OSWorld 2.0 result at just over a third of the cost. Anthropic's own page concedes Opus 5 'remains substantially behind Mythos 5' on cybersecurity exploit development, and ships cyber classifiers that intervene 'around 85% less often' than Fable 5's -- a safety posture explicitly tied to the narrower capability.

Researcher Chaofan Shou claims Kimi K3, coordinating 32 specialized agents, found 19 Redis zero-days in about 90 minutes and built a working Redis 8.8.0 remote-code-execution exploit in 27 minutes, spanning a Streams shared-NACK use-after-free and a RedisBloom TDigest out-of-bounds write. Redis shipped seven security patches in response, but the counts, timings, and claimed autonomy remain entirely self-reported -- no independent reproduction exists yet, and Redis's own CVE record doesn't match the claimed bug classes one-to-one.

India's Cyber Crime Coordination Centre ordered GitHub to remove three repositories of Jack Dorsey's Bitchat (a Bluetooth-mesh, no-account, no-server encrypted chat app) within three hours, arguing its offline-communication capability itself -- not any specific illegal content -- 'creates a substantial risk of misuse.' The order lands amid a student protest movement where the government has repeatedly cut mobile internet; digital-rights lawyers call the legal basis unclear for targeting an entire open-source project over its architecture.

block/buzz, a Rust 'hive mind communication platform,' accelerated to +3,270 GitHub stars/day (10,312 total) today -- up from its 07-24 debut of +2,162/day (7,449 total), a genuine second-day acceleration rather than the typical post-launch decay curve, and now GitHub Trending's #1 repo two days running.

Cognition acquired The Interaction Company of California (makers of Poke, a messaging-native AI assistant) for a deal valued in the low nine figures, explicitly to bring Poke's conversational style into its coding agent Devin. Separately, Midjourney acquired Co-Star, a social astrology app with 4.3 million monthly active users -- both deals target interaction style and personality rather than model capability or infrastructure, the opposite acquisition logic from typical AI-lab M&A.

Automattic/harper, an offline privacy-first Rust grammar checker, debuted on GitHub Trending at +876 stars/day (13,096 total) -- a systems-language substitute for cloud writing-assistance SaaS, extending the open-alternative-to-SaaS pattern this stream has tracked in dev tooling and SEO/deployment infra into a new category.

r/LocalLLaMA reports Gemma 4 26B A4B running on an iPhone 17 Pro via model paging -- a concrete mobile-deployment data point for a 26B-parameter model on consumer hardware, though unverified beyond a single Reddit post with no published benchmark numbers.

Two Tildes ~tech discourse threads extend the standing privacy-demand pattern without Play Store chart conversion: 'A hacker's arrest reveals Microsoft can track users via a Windows device' and 'Protect your privacy with California's DROP tool' -- both high-engagement discourse, zero effect yet on Play Store's top-30, where Signal (#27) and Proton Mail (#24) remain down-chart.

takeaway.text: A frontier model launch that openly concedes a capability gap, an open-weight competitor's unverified claim to have closed that exact gap the same day, a government ordering a privacy app's source code removed for working as designed, and two AI labs acquiring consumer apps purely for their personality layer -- capability, security, and trust are all being renegotiated in public at once today.
